verdict.rationale: Luma ships a first-party API with SDKs covering image and video generation. Some advanced UI features are explicitly exposed there, including Multi-Keyframe sequence control and HDR/16-bit EXR output. However, nothing documents parity with the UI. The API is described as just two endpoints, and UI features such as Luma Agents, Skills, Modify Video V2, Reframe and motion transfer are not shown to be API-accessible. Missing for 10: an explicit UI/API parity statement, API coverage of Agents/Skills/Modify/Reframe/motion transfer, a published OpenAPI spec (probe returned 404), and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: Dream Machine API let's developers use image and video generation capabilities.
Sequence-level control, exposed at the API.
Native HDR Generation and 16-bit EXR Export so AI work composites alongside live-action plates in your users' Resolve or Nuke.
Luma API: Two endpoints, Python/JS/TS SDKs, credit-based pricing, production-grade from day one
